paper.title_en: Zero modes of non-abelian Dirac operator in topologically non-trivial band insulator
paper.abstract_en: We show that the local gauge-invariance of the quantum geometric tensor (QGT) defined in the two-dimensional Block-momentum (BM) space of a generic $N$-band (arising out of sub-lattice degrees of freedom) insulator represented by a tight-binding hamiltonian, leads to the existence of zero modes of non-abelian Dirac operator in such BM space. These zero modes in the two-dimensional Brillouin zone torus $T^{2}$, determines the probability amplitudes associated with the $N$-component ground state wave-function under adiabatic approximation. We analytically derive the expansion coefficients of maximally localized Wannier function in one-dimension from the solutions of these zero mode equations, and obtain momentum-space generalization of celebrated Laughlin gauge condition as a by-product.The commutator of these non-abelian Dirac operators define the algebra of the guiding center co-ordinates which provide a more general frame-work to study such systems than one based on the Landau-level analogues. In the ideal quantum geometric limit, these zero-mode solutions become self-dual momentum-space instantons, and can be linked to the non-abelian generalization of the vortexability criterion of Chern bands in momentum-space. We derive some exact solutions of such zero-mode on the complex torus geometry, and discuss implications of this framework for realistic systems such as two-dimensional topological insulators, rhombohedral $N_{L}$-layer graphene.
